stem:
Navya has a metal bar with clear length, width, and height. Kabir has an irregular clay lump. A measuring cylinder with water is on the bench. Each needs the volume of their object.

Which claims correctly match object to volume method? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Navya can find the bar's volume as length times width times height.
Kabir should use length times width times height on the clay lump because volume always needs three edge lengths.
Kabir can find the clay lump's volume from the rise in water level in the measuring cylinder.
Navya must ignore the bar's edges and use only water displacement, because every solid needs the cylinder.

teacher.key_rationale: A regular bar with measurable edges uses l×w×h. An irregular clay lump needs water displacement. Forcing three edges on an irregular solid, or forcing displacement on a measurable cuboid, misapplies the rule.
